Create a complete, single-file classic Snake game (HTML+CSS+JS all in this one .html file, no external dependencies). Requirements:

GRID & RENDERING
- 30x30 grid rendered on an HTML5 <canvas> (each cell 20px, canvas size 600x600), centered on the page with a dark theme (dark background, neon-ish snake/food colors, subtle grid lines).
- Continuous movement: each snake moves one cell per game tick in its current direction (fixed-interval game loop via setInterval/requestAnimationFrame with tick throttling, e.g. ~120ms per tick, using two separate directional state variables: current direction and a queued/pending next direction to prevent instant 180-degree reversal into itself).
- Snake grows by one segment when it eats food; food is placed randomly on an empty cell (never on a snake body).
- Collision detection: hitting a wall (going outside 0..29 on x or y) or hitting any part of its own body or the other snake's body (when two snakes are in play) ends that snake / ends the game.

GAME STATES (a simple state machine): 'menu' -> 'playing' -> 'gameover', with functions to transition between them and separate full-screen overlay <div>s for menu and game-over screen that are shown/hidden (not separate pages).

START MENU
- Title "SNAKE" plus instructions.
- Three selectable game modes as buttons AND selectable via keyboard (1/2/3 keys) plus Enter to start:
  1. Human vs Human (two players on same keyboard: Player 1 = Arrow keys, Player 2 = WASD)
  2. CPU vs Human (one CPU snake, one human-controlled snake; human uses Arrow keys or WASD)
  3. CPU vs CPU (both snakes AI-controlled, fully automatic, spectator mode)
- Also support a plain single-snake practice mode is NOT required — only implement exactly these 3 two-snake modes as requested, but if only one human/one CPU is needed for a mode just don't spawn a second snake's controls.
  Actually: implement exactly 3 modes as listed above, always with two snakes on the board (except that is fine since all 3 modes are 2-snake modes).
- Clicking a mode button or pressing 1/2/3 then Enter (or clicking directly starts immediately) begins the game in that mode.

CONTROLS
- Player 1 (human, Arrow keys: ArrowUp/Down/Left/Right).
- Player 2 (human, WASD: W/A/S/D) — used in Human vs Human mode, and also usable as the human player's alternate control scheme in CPU vs Human mode (accept both WASD and Arrow keys for the single human in that mode).
- Prevent default browser scrolling behavior for arrow keys/WASD/space via preventDefault on keydown.
- Pressing Enter or Space restarts the game from the game-over screen or start menu (goes back to / restarts with the same or menu selection). On game-over screen, pressing Enter/Space returns to the start menu (or directly restarts last mode — restart with a keypress as requested); also include an on-screen "Press ENTER to play again" hint.

CPU AI (for CPU-controlled snakes)
- Implement pathfinding: use BFS (breadth-first search) over the 30x30 grid from the CPU snake's head to the food, treating cells occupied by any snake body as obstacles (except the CPU's own tail cell, which will move away, can be treated as free to allow tighter maneuvering — simple approach: mark all current body segments except the very last tail segment as blocked).
- If a BFS path to the food exists, take the first step of that path as the next direction.
- If no path exists (food unreachable/trapped), fall back to a survival heuristic: pick the legal adjacent move (not a wall, not a body) that maximizes reachable free space via a flood-fill/BFS count from that candidate cell (choose the move keeping the CPU alive longest / most open space). If truly no legal move exists, keep current direction (will die next tick).
- CPU recomputes its move every tick before moving.

SCORING & HUD
- During gameplay show a HUD bar above or over the canvas with each snake's score (score = segments eaten, or body length - starting length) labeled clearly, e.g. "Player 1: 3" / "CPU: 5", colored to match each snake's color, plus current mode name.
- Track high score in-memory (not required to persist) optionally.

GAME OVER
- When a snake dies (wall/self/other-snake collision), end the game (both snakes stop). Determine winner: if in a two-snake mode, the surviving snake (or higher score if both die same tick / simultaneous head-on collision) wins; handle simultaneous death as a draw.
- Show full-screen game-over overlay with: result text (e.g. "Player 1 Wins!", "CPU Wins!", "Draw!"), final scores for both snakes, and "Press ENTER or SPACE to return to Menu" / restart hint.

CODE STRUCTURE
- Plain vanilla JS, no external libraries/CDNs, everything inline in <style> and <script> tags within this one .html file.
- Reasonably organized: a Snake class/object (body array of {x,y}, direction, pendingDirection, alive, color, score, isCPU flag, controls key mapping), a Food object/position, a Game controller object holding state ('menu'|'playing'|'gameover'), mode, snakes array, tick()/update()/draw()/render() functions, BFS pathfinding helper function, flood-fill helper function, keydown event listener that behaves differently depending on game state, and the setInterval game loop.
- Use requestAnimationFrame for rendering combined with a fixed-timestep accumulator for logic ticks, OR simply use setInterval for logic ticks (simplest, acceptable) — pick the simpler setInterval approach for the tick and just draw every tick.
- Add clear code comments explaining each section (grid setup, snake class, CPU AI/BFS, game loop, input handling, rendering, menu/gameover UI logic).

Produce the entire file content now (doctype, html, head with title "Snake Game" and inline <style>, body with canvas + menu overlay + gameover overlay + HUD, inline <script> with all logic).
"}
